name: H3maxai
subcategory: thin AI wrapper, exact function unclear
tagline: A small AI web product that wraps a hosted model behind a branded single-purpose interface.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: There is very little verifiable public detail about this one, so treat the whole entry as provisional. What is visible is the standard shape of a small AI web product: a hosted model, a prompt layer, a credit or subscription wall, and a tidy single-purpose UI. That shape is close to the easiest thing an agent can one-shot, because the intelligence is rented from an API that you can rent too. The honest gap is that nobody can say which prompt chain, fine-tune, or dataset sits behind the wall, and if the answer is a genuinely tuned model then your clone will be visibly worse. Build it, compare outputs side by side, and keep whichever one you actually use.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that takes your input, runs it through your own prompt chain against a model API key you supply, and stores the results in a searchable history.
requirements: Your own model API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar)
Node 20 and a place to run it, local or a cheap VPS
Willingness to pay per token instead of per month
whatYouLose: Whatever prompt engineering or fine-tuning is hidden behind their wall, which you cannot see and therefore cannot copy
A hosted URL that works on your phone without you touching deploy configs
Any usage limits, rate limiting, and abuse handling that comes free with someone else's infrastructure
Updates when the underlying model changes and the old prompts start misbehaving
The polished output formatting that makes these products feel better than a raw API call
moatNotes: Unverified. If the model is just an API call with a system prompt, there is no moat at all; if it is tuned on something they own, there is one and you will notice.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a working URL beats a repo. Most buyers of small AI products are not paying for the model, they are paying to skip the API key, the billing setup, the prompt iteration, and the twenty minutes of fiddling that stand between them and one answer. A monthly fee is a rounding error against that friction for anyone who uses the thing occasionally, and the DIY version only wins if you use it often enough to care.
notes: Filed with low confidence: the public surface is thin enough that the clone is partly a guess at what you are cloning.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user AI workspace web app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3. One repo, runs with npm install and npm run dev.

Secrets: read OPENAI_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) from .env.local. Commit a .env.example. Never hardcode a key. If the key is missing, show a clear banner instead of crashing.

Core loop:
1. A single page with a large input area, an optional 'mode' select, and a Run button.
2. Modes are defined in one editable file, config/modes.ts, each with a name, a system prompt, and a temperature. Ship three starter modes and make it obvious how to add more.
3. On Run, POST to /api/run, which calls the model API with the selected system prompt and streams the response back.
4. Stream tokens into the result pane as they arrive. Show a stop button while streaming.
5. Persist every run to SQLite: id, timestamp, mode, input, output, model, token counts if available.

History:
- A sidebar listing past runs, newest first, with a text search over input and output.
- Clicking a run loads it into the view, read only, with a 'rerun with current prompt' button.
- Delete a run. Export all runs as JSON.

Prompt editing:
- A settings page where I can edit mode system prompts in the browser and save them to the database, overriding the file defaults. Include a reset-to-default button.

In scope: streaming, history, search, prompt editing, JSON export, keyboard shortcut for Run (cmd+enter).
Out of scope: auth, multi-user, payments, usage quotas, mobile app, RAG, file uploads, any vector database.

Deliver a README with setup in under ten lines and one paragraph on cost per run.
